I definitely want to see voat grow, but I don't want it to become resentful like reddit did. The problem is that is almost unavoidable if we ever have a userbase the size of reddit, but I believe that, if handled properly, Voat can overcome a lot of these pitfalls.

The biggest problems I foresee are vote manipulation and concentration of default subs. With a large user base, Voat will definitely fall victim to vote manipulation schemes, and its up to the admins to combat it effectively.

Even though a large user base almost guarantees shitposts, if Voat can encourage users to branch out into many subs, it can at least preserve the small community feeling to some degree. I want to see Voat grow, but it needs to be handled very carefully to avoid the pitfalls reddit fell into.

I don't go on the internet to change the world, I go for entertainment and education (and porn... mostly porn.). I don't think voat needs to get as big as reddit to provide those things for me but I certainly hope it grows but grows in "good" ways. What I mean by that is I hope we can foster an environment were quality OC is produced and appreciated. I hope honest and open discussions became a mainstay of this site. I hope it becomes a more mature reddit, or maybe what reddit used to be.
Small. I wrote a really long post that made the decision a very close one as I noticed the contradictions of choosing one. That being said, I choose small, I've hardly met those already here.
We should encourage growth if it involves intelligence and open-mindedness, but smaller, exclusive communities tend to have better discussion and content.
I want it to become bigger than Reddit, more powerful, more influential, but in the right direction. I don't want an oligopoly on massive main subverses, but rather across various smaller subverses.

I never what to see 7228 comments on a single post. I don't even want to see half that many. Reddit is so big of the 7228 comments on one post less then a quarter ever see an upvote, downvote or response. Its throwing bytes to the wind. I like seeing 50 to 200 comments.
I'd prefer it to become a place of smaller, tight knit communities that produce quality content.
